exercises.title: Fix Third-Person Auxiliary
exercises.prompt: Correct the auxiliary verb error in the sentence below while preserving the original meaning.
exercises.original_context: She don't understand why the schedule changed so abruptly.
exercises.target_sentence: She doesn't understand why the schedule changed so abruptly.

hints.text: Remember: for singular third-person subjects (he, she, it), standard English uses 'does/doesn't', not 'do/don't'.
Replace the word 'don't' with 'doesn't'.
Model answer: She doesn't understand why the schedule changed so abruptly.

accepted_answers: She doesn't understand why the schedule changed so abruptly.
She does not understand why the schedule changed so abruptly.

exercises.title: Fix Auxiliary Verb Construction 'was do'
exercises.prompt: Correct the incorrect auxiliary verb construction 'was do'. Depending on context, use simple past ('did') or past continuous ('was doing').
exercises.original_context: I was do it by myself yesterday afternoon.
exercises.target_sentence: I did it by myself yesterday afternoon.
constraints: Replace 'was do' with correct past tense verb form

hints.text: The auxiliary 'was' cannot be followed directly by a base verb like 'do'.
For a completed past action, replace 'was do' with the simple past 'did'.
Model answer: I did it by myself yesterday afternoon.

accepted_answers: I did it by myself yesterday afternoon.
I was doing it by myself yesterday afternoon.

exercises.title: Modal Verb with Bare Infinitive
exercises.prompt: Remove the unnecessary preposition following the modal verb.
exercises.original_context: All employees must to submit their weekly timesheets by Friday.
exercises.target_sentence: All employees must submit their weekly timesheets by Friday.

hints.text: Modal auxiliary verbs (can, could, must, should, will, would) take the base verb directly without 'to'.
Delete the word 'to' between 'must' and 'submit'.
Model answer: All employees must submit their weekly timesheets by Friday.

accepted_answers: All employees must submit their weekly timesheets by Friday.

exercises.title: Preposition Collocation: Depend
exercises.prompt: Correct the incorrect preposition that follows the verb 'depend'.
exercises.original_context: Our future growth will depend of how well we innovate.
exercises.target_sentence: Our future growth will depend on how well we innovate.
constraints: Use the correct preposition that collocates with 'depend'

hints.text: The verb 'depend' always collocates with 'on' or 'upon', not 'of'.
Change 'depend of' to 'depend on'.
Model answer: Our future growth will depend on how well we innovate.

accepted_answers: Our future growth will depend on how well we innovate.
Our future growth will depend upon how well we innovate.

exercises.title: Combine with Relative Clause
exercises.prompt: Combine the two sentences into one fluent sentence using a relative clause with 'who'.
exercises.original_context: Dr. Sarah Miller is a renowned researcher. She discovered the novel compound.
exercises.target_sentence: Dr. Sarah Miller is a renowned researcher who discovered the novel compound.

hints.text: Use 'who' to connect the person with what she did without repeating 'She'.
Replace '. She' with ' who '.
Model answer: Dr. Sarah Miller is a renowned researcher who discovered the novel compound.

accepted_answers: Dr. Sarah Miller is a renowned researcher who discovered the novel compound.
Dr. Sarah Miller, who is a renowned researcher, discovered the novel compound.

exercises.title: Idiomatic Polish
exercises.prompt: Rewrite this awkward literal translation into natural, idiomatic English.
exercises.original_context: We made a big discussion about this topic yesterday night.
exercises.target_sentence: We had an extensive discussion about this topic last night.
constraints: Avoid 'made a big discussion' and 'yesterday night'

hints.text: In English, we 'have a discussion' (not 'make') and say 'last night' (not 'yesterday night').
Change 'made a big discussion' to 'had a detailed/extensive discussion' and 'yesterday night' to 'last night'.
Model answer: We had an in-depth discussion about this topic last night.

accepted_answers: We had an in-depth discussion about this topic last night.
We had an extensive discussion about this topic last night.
We had a long discussion about this topic last night.
We had a thorough discussion about this topic last night.

exercises.title: Elevate to Formal Register
exercises.prompt: Transform this casual message into a formal professional email sentence.
exercises.original_context: Hey guys, can you please send me the file asap?
exercises.target_sentence: Could you please provide the requested document at your earliest convenience?
constraints: Do not use casual greetings ('Hey guys')

hints.text: Use polite modal expressions like 'Could you please...' and replace 'asap' with 'at your earliest convenience'.
Begin with 'Could you please provide...' and conclude with 'at your earliest convenience?'
Model answer: Could you please provide the requested file at your earliest convenience?

accepted_answers: Could you please provide the requested file at your earliest convenience?
Could you please forward the document at your earliest convenience?
Could you please send the requested file at your earliest convenience?

exercises.title: Enhance Discourse Cohesion
exercises.prompt: Insert an appropriate transitional adverb (such as 'Furthermore', 'However', or 'Consequently') to connect these contrasting claims.
exercises.original_context: The initial cost of solar installation is substantial. The long-term energy savings significantly outweigh the initial investment.
exercises.target_sentence: The initial cost of solar installation is substantial; however, the long-term energy savings significantly outweigh the initial investment.
constraints: Use a contrastive transition word such as 'However' or 'Nevertheless'
Ensure correct punctuation around the transition

hints.text: The second sentence contrasts with the first. Use a contrast marker like 'However' or 'Nevertheless'.
Place 'However,' at the beginning of the second sentence.
Model answer: The initial cost of solar installation is substantial. However, the long-term energy savings significantly outweigh the initial investment.

accepted_answers: The initial cost of solar installation is substantial. However, the long-term energy savings significantly outweigh the initial investment.
The initial cost of solar installation is substantial; however, the long-term energy savings significantly outweigh the initial investment.
The initial cost of solar installation is substantial. Nevertheless, the long-term energy savings significantly outweigh the initial investment.

exercises.title: Expand Sentence with Contextual Modifiers
exercises.prompt: Expand the simple sentence by adding descriptive details (location, timing, or manner) while keeping the core meaning intact.
exercises.target_sentence: The express train arrived promptly at the crowded central station amid heavy morning rain.
constraints: Expand the core clause 'The train arrived'
Include at least one descriptive modifier or location phrase

hints.text: Add modifiers answering when, where, or how the train arrived.
Specify what kind of train it was and which station it reached.
Model answer: The express train arrived promptly at the crowded central station amid heavy morning rain.

accepted_answers: The express train arrived promptly at the crowded central station amid heavy morning rain.
The morning train arrived at the busy station on time.
The express train arrived on time at the busy station.

exercises.title: Paraphrase Complex Statement
exercises.prompt: Paraphrase the statement using different grammatical structures and synonyms while maintaining the exact original meaning.
exercises.original_context: Although the project faced severe budget constraints, the team delivered it on schedule.
exercises.target_sentence: Despite significant financial limitations, the team completed the project on time.

hints.text: Use 'Despite' or 'In spite of' followed by a noun phrase instead of 'Although'.
Replace 'budget constraints' with 'financial limitations' and 'delivered it on schedule' with 'completed the project on time'.
Model answer: Despite significant financial limitations, the team completed the project on time.

accepted_answers: Despite significant financial limitations, the team completed the project on time.
In spite of severe financial limitations, the team finished the project on schedule.
Despite facing severe budget limitations, the team finished the project on time.
